cards.name: Tune Blur
cards.summary: Interactive blur picker: the dialog shows four preview thumbnails (Gaussian, Smooth, Directional Smooth, Soften) and each click on one adds that kind of blur by the Step amount, so you build up a soft, slightly out-of-focus look while comparing the four kinds side by side.
use_for: softening a background photo behind a headline when you are not sure which blur reads best
taking the hard digital edge off an upscaled or over-sharpened bitmap
building a gentle soft-focus in small, previewed steps
avoid: scripting: the harvested command sets only Step; the four thumbnails (ImageNode_* keys) carry no harvested values and are what actually add blur in the dialog, so a scripted Step on its own may change nothing; use Effects > Blur > Gaussian Blur when a script needs a known radius
a strong, exact blur: one click adds only one Step, and the amount is easier to control with Gaussian Blur's radius
the already-soft PGD photo plate: small steps barely show; the crisp colour strip and hairlines at the bottom show it first

scripts: no scripted form applies it (2026-10-13 probe (44 forms: ListSize plus per-step Effect_n / Step_n / Percentage_n / Level_n keys, the sub-effect command names, the dialog thumbnail guids, the data-source route): TuneBlurEffect raised RPC_E_SERVERFAULT on every form); open the dialog (menu route) and pick the thumbnails by hand

params.name: Step
params.does: how much blur each click on a thumbnail adds
params.typical: 10 (default) for fine control, 30-100 for big jumps

params.name: ImageNode_Gaussian
params.does: the Gaussian thumbnail: click to add an even, round blur

params.name: ImageNode_Smooth
params.does: the Smooth thumbnail: click to add a mild averaging blur that keeps more detail

params.name: ImageNode_DirectionalSmooth
params.does: the Directional Smooth thumbnail: smooths flat areas while trying to keep edges

params.name: ImageNode_Soften
params.does: the Soften thumbnail: click to soften harsh edges with a subtle blur

pairs_with: Effects > Blur > Gaussian Blur (exact radius once you know the look)
Effects > Correction > Tune Sharpen (same click-to-add dialog for sharpening)
Transparency tool (fade the blurred copy into a sharp original)

cards.name: Zoom
cards.summary: Zoom blur: streaks pixels outward from a centre point as if the lens zoomed during the exposure, leaving the centre fairly sharp and the edges smeared into radial speed lines.
use_for: speed / impact backgrounds behind a product or headline
pulling the eye to the centre of a poster photo
action and sports graphics with a burst-of-motion feel
avoid: text or faces near the frame edge: they streak first and become unreadable
an off-centre subject: the centre point is picked in the dialog and is not a harvested key, so a script zooms from the default centre (not verified which)
a circular spin instead of an outward burst: use Effects > Blur > Radial Blur

cards.name: Colorize
cards.summary: Replaces every colour in the bitmap with one hue at one saturation while keeping each pixel's lightness, so the image becomes a single-colour (duotone-like) tint, e.g. all blue or all sepia-brown.
use_for: brand-colour photo treatments behind type
making mismatched stock photos read as one set
monochrome hero images for posters and social cards
avoid: keeping any original colour: everything, including skin tones and strong reds, becomes the one hue
Saturation 0 (the default): the result is plain greyscale; raise Saturation to see the tint
a two-colour duotone with separate shadow and highlight colours: use a duotone or tone curve instead

params.name: Saturation

cards.name: Diffuse
cards.summary: Camera-style diffusion: spreads neighbouring pixels into each other so detail and noise soften, like a soft-focus or diffusion lens; higher Level spreads further. A 1:1 render (Level 100) shows a smooth, even spread, not a speckle: hard edges blur over about 3-5 px while the soft photo moves by about 1 level.
use_for: soft, dreamy portrait or wedding photo backgrounds
hiding JPEG noise or harsh detail in a background photo
taking the digital crispness off a bitmap before placing type over it
avoid: the already-soft PGD photo plate: the change mostly shows on the crisp colour strip, type and hairlines at the bottom
a controlled, even blur: use Effects > Blur > Gaussian Blur
a frosted-glass / pixel-scatter look: the 1:1 render shows a smooth spread with no random scatter, so it does not give that look

params.name: Level
params.does: how far pixels are spread

pairs_with: Effects > Blur > Gaussian Blur
Effects > Camera > Sepia Toning (old soft-focus photo)
Transparency tool (mix with a sharp copy)

cards.name: Lens Flare
cards.summary: Renders a camera lens flare on the bitmap: a bright flare core with halo, star rays, streaks, an anamorphic light bar and a tail of reflection rings, each with its own controls (size, brightness, falloff, rotation, ray count, colour, depending on the element). A Preset list holds ready-made flares (Default, 105mm Prime, 35mm Prime, and in the preset harvest more such as Nuclear Blast, Star Explosion and coloured Sun Rays).
use_for: sun / spotlight glare on posters, movie-style key art and event banners
cinematic anamorphic light streaks on dark photos
adding a light source that ties a composite together
avoid: placement: the flare's position has no harvested key, so a script puts it wherever the effect defaults; the colours (FlareColorItem etc.) are not in the command string either
light, busy photos: the flare washes out; it reads best over darker areas
a vector flare that stays editable at any size: Illustrator's Flare Tool or a CorelDRAW gradient object

cards.name: Spot Filter
cards.summary: Centre-spot focus filter: the middle of the picture stays sharp while the surround is blurred and darkened more and more toward the edges, with a gradual (feathered) transition, like a photographer's centre-spot lens. use_for: drawing the eye to a centred subject in a photo

cards.name: Time Machine
cards.summary: Restyles the bitmap as a photo from a historical process: Daguerreotype, Albumen, Cyanotype, Platinum, Early Color, Box Camera or Cross Process, each with its own toning, contrast and ageing; Intensity sets the strength and Photo edges adds a worn photographic border.
use_for: period looks for history posts, heritage campaigns and invitations

cards.scripting: ActiveLayer.Import("<PGD folder>\media\plate_photo.png") (returns nothing; the imported bitmap is then ActiveShape), s = ActiveShape, then s.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect("Time Machine", "TimeMachineEffect Intensity=100,PhotoEdges=true") (style left as the dialog holds it; bool spelling not confirmed). The command format is proven on 6 other effects but this effect's string was never applied in a test (the harvest's Pixelate and Invert strings returned OK and changed no pixels), so compare pixels before and after. Menu route (opens the dialog, values chosen by hand): Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("5de003a1-28f9-4dba-bd00-aecc39acb1f6").
cards.non_destructive: yes from the menu: CorelDRAW 2024 keeps the effect in the object's effect stack where it can be edited, hidden or deleted; the scripted Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect path appears to write into the bitmap itself (the harvest's apply tests saw pixels change and Undo restore them)
